name: SIGINT
standfirst: Security research and practitioner news, scored for novelty and actionability.
colophon: sigint.wtf — the correct response to most of these CVEs. Scored by machine against a hand-written rubric; ranking is opinion, not fact.

items.title: CosmosEscape: Taking over Every Database in Azure Cosmos DB
items.dek: Authentication bypass in Azure Cosmos DB allows account takeover across all databases via connection string exposure in error messages.
items.unproven: whether Wiz disclosed responsibly before publication; whether Microsoft has issued patches or workarounds for existing deployments

items.title: Piggybacking on Perception: Stealthy Concurrent Audio Prompt Injections against Multimodal LLM Agents
items.dek: Concurrent audio prompt injections using instruction augmentation and scenario concealment achieve 69% attack success on Gemini 3 Pro and GPT-4o-audio.
items.unproven: Evaluation limited to audio-in multimodal agents; does not test whether agents in SDLC pipelines (code review, architecture analysis) inherit the same vulnerability.

items.title: Agent Harness Distillation: Inference-Time Harness Extraction and Exploitation in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
items.dek: Black-box extraction of inference-time harnesses in LLM multi-agent systems leaks operational coordination logic and decision patterns.
items.unproven: Framework and threat model presented; no measurements of what fraction of real AMAS harnesses are extractable or whether defenses exist.

items.title: Safeguards Based on Copyable Context Cannot Provide Reliable Safety for LLMs
items.dek: LLM safety guardrails decide before seeing downstream use; copyable context cannot guarantee safety without hard-to-copy credentials.
items.unproven: whether credential-based mitigations are implementable within existing commercial LLM guardrail tooling.

items.title: Don't Trust the AI Ecosystem: Analyzing Privacy Leakage in Compromised Open-Source Components
items.dek: GradLock embeds pixel-perfect training data into model weights via compromised supply chains, extracting with near-lossless fidelity.
items.unproven: robustness against federated learning or other gradient obfuscation; detection feasibility during code review or model inspection.

items.title: Tailscale didn't stop the Hugging Face intrusion
items.dek: Hugging Face intrusion proceeded despite Tailscale deployment, indicating VPN alone insufficient for supply-chain protection.
items.unproven: whether Tailscale was misconfigured, what the actual attack vector was, or how this generalizes beyond this incident

items.title: Emerging Challenges in Threat Modeling for GenAI-Augmented Systems: A View from the Trenches
items.authors: Nicolás E. Díaz Ferreyra et al.
items.dek: Three threat-modeling methods applied to GenAI systems in SME; gaps identified in supply-chain and human-centered risk categories.
items.unproven: generalizability beyond single case study; maturity and adoption readiness of methods for application-security teams

items.title: Old Tricks, New Models: How Simple Image Transformations Break Modern AI-based Content Moderation
items.dek: Simple image transformations—color inversion, grayscale, rotation—bypass three commercial multimodal content-moderation APIs at scale.
items.unproven: Black-box evaluation of public APIs only; does not establish whether this reflects architectural flaws or tuning gaps in the reader's own deployment.

items.title: Benign on Label, Malicious by Design: Clean-Label Dormant-to-Activated Backdoor via Machine Unlearning with Removable Camouflage
items.dek: Machine unlearning can activate dormant clean-label backdoors injected at training time, bypassing post-training detection.
items.unproven: whether the attack survives standard model quantization, pruning, or other deployment optimizations; transferability across model families.

items.title: RFC 10015: Deprecating Obsolete Key Exchange Methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2
items.dek: RFC 10015 proposes deprecating obsolete key exchange methods in TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2.
items.unproven: does not establish timeline for enforcement or impact on legacy systems the reader must support

items.title: Statistically secure uncloneable encryption of arbitrary messages
items.dek: Statistically secure uncloneable encryption extended to arbitrary message length; theoretical contribution without deployment path.
items.unproven: no evidence of practical implementation or comparison to existing key material protection schemes; no timeline for quantum hardware capable of the required operations

items.title: Optimal T Counts under Sparsity: from QROM to State Preparation and Block Encoding
items.dek: Optimal T-count bounds for sparse quantum read-only memory scale as Θ(√sm + √sn), matching lower bounds.
items.unproven: no experimental validation on quantum hardware; theoretical result only

items.title: Security of World-Model-Based Embodied AI: A Lifecycle of Threats, Defenses, and Evaluation
items.dek: Survey maps attack families—poisoning, backdoors, adversarial examples—onto world-model lifecycle in embodied AI systems.
items.unproven: Taxonomy paper without new attacks, defenses, or measurements; vocabulary only for an emerging threat surface the reader does not yet own.

items.title: Efficient atom rearrangements for quantum error correction primitives with a single AOD
items.dek: Logarithmic AOD stroke count for atom rearrangements reduces 90° rotation from O(d²) to O(log d) using geometric decompositions.
items.unproven: implementation on neutral-atom hardware and integration with full error correction codes not demonstrated

items.title: Checking Information Flow in Cloud-based IoT Access Control Policies (Extended Version)
items.dek: SMT-based tool verifies unwanted information flow in AWS IoT Core access control policies via reachability analysis.
items.unproven: Tool evaluated on one realistic scenario and unspecified real-world policies; scalability to large deployments and comparison to commercial IoT policy checkers not shown.

items.title: Temporal Poisoning: Clean-Label Backdoors via Event Redistribution in SNNs
items.dek: Clean-label backdoor attack on Spiking Neural Networks via temporal event redistribution achieves 100% attack success rate.
items.unproven: SNNs are niche hardware; no evidence this threatens systems the reader deploys or must defend, and no practical mitigation beyond rate-collapse defenses.

items.title: Deterministic QKD source robust against side-channel attacks
items.dek: QKD source architecture eliminates need for post-selection or extinction ratio constraints while resisting Trojan-horse attacks.
items.unproven: no laboratory demonstration; relies on unvalidated assumptions about practical device imperfections

items.title: Exponential Advantage of Multipartite Entanglement over Quantum Communication with Applications to Bounded-Storage Cryptography
items.dek: Multipartite entanglement achieves exponential communication advantage over quantum communication alone; cryptographic separation shown in randomness extraction.
items.unproven: physical implementation feasibility; practical cryptographic deployment against real adversaries; whether bounded-storage assumptions hold post-quantum.

items.title: Witness robustness: An operational quantifier of measurement resources via free state discrimination
items.dek: Witness robustness quantifies measurement advantage in free-state discrimination and vanishes when resource-destroying maps exist.
items.unproven: whether operational interpretation applies beyond the measurement-discrimination setting; practical use in resource-theory optimization; faithfulness conditions in common theories.

items.title: CHARGE: Leveraging CWE Hierarchies for Hardware Security SystemVerilog Assertion Generation
items.dek: LLM-driven SystemVerilog assertion generation using CWE hierarchies detects 27 of 42 bugs in open-source SoC designs.
items.unproven: false-positive rates and vacuity analysis on proprietary RTL; whether generated assertions integrate into existing hardware security workflows without manual triage.

items.title: Scanning 7.6 Petabytes of HuggingFace Training Data for Secrets
items.dek: Truffle Security scanned HuggingFace data for exposed secrets; found many, no novel detection method disclosed.
items.unproven: Whether findings represent actual exploitable credentials versus false positives; no methodology for remediation or impact assessment provided.

items.title: Just brute force your embeddings
items.dek: Brute-force search over embeddings as a baseline for vector retrieval; known technique applied to a specific corpus.
items.unproven: Whether this scales to production embedding dimensions and corpora; whether computational cost trades favorably against indexed retrieval in realistic deployments.

items.title: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations
items.dek: Anthropic documents three real-world cybersecurity incidents found during AI model evaluations; incident taxonomy adds vocabulary, no immediate tooling change.
items.unproven: No disclosure of which evaluations, what findings changed in practice, or whether incidents apply to agents entering SDLC processes.

items.title: Quantum Fidelity-per-Cost: A Metric for Evaluation of Quantum Computing Systems
items.dek: Cross-provider measurement of 12 quantum processors and cost-aware scoring metric; no action for non-quantum teams.
items.unproven: limited to current NISQ hardware offerings; does not address cryptographically relevant quantum capability timelines or post-quantum migration strategy

items.title: Implementing Homomorphic Encryption-Based Logic Locking in System-on-Chip Designs
items.dek: Logic locking for RISC-V SoC using homomorphic encryption; 6% LUT overhead, 2.6µs unlock latency.
items.unproven: evaluation on attack scenarios beyond parameterization exposure; threat model scope limited to privilege-switching paths

noise.title: Agent Skill to Force Docs in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English
noise.dek: GitHub repository adds agent skill to produce simplified technical English; tool development not tied to SAST/DAST/SCA or SDLC process.

noise.title: Making Postgres queues scale
noise.dek: Database-backed queue patterns; engineering blog on scaling Postgres for job dispatch.
noise.unproven: outside the reader's remit; not an application security finding

noise.title: Algorithms on billion-scale graph using 10GB RAM: I love DataFusion
noise.dek: Engineering blog post on using DataFusion for graph processing demonstrates a tool capability, not a security finding.
